title: Capacity, runbooks and safe operations
summary: Size disks and consumer fleets from numbers, work the classic incidents (lag, DLQ pile-up, full disk, rebalance storm) from a runbook, and run offset resets, reassignments and rolling restarts without making things worse.

steps.title: Capacity planning with numbers
body: Capacity questions have arithmetic answers. Do the sums before the incident does them for you.
**Kafka disk per broker**
```text
ingress 20 MB/s  x  retention 7 days (604 800 s)  x  replication factor 3  /  6 brokers
= 6 048 000 MB = 6 048 GB of data per broker
keep disks at most ~70% full (headroom for a broker loss, rebalancing, retention lag)
-> provision 6 048 / 0.70 = 8 640 GB per broker
- Retention is **time-based but deletes whole segments**, so add one `segment.bytes` per partition on top.
- When a broker dies, its partitions' traffic moves to the others: plan for N-1 brokers carrying the load.
**Consumers**
```text
peak 3 000 msg/s, one consumer handles 400 msg/s  ->  ceil(3000 / 400) = 8 consumers
8 consumers need >= 8 partitions; 15 consumers on 12 partitions = 3 idle
**RabbitMQ**: queues are meant to be short. Size memory and disk for the **worst backlog you accept** (a consumer
outage of N minutes x the publish rate x message size), remember that quorum queues keep every message on disk on 3
nodes, and set `disk_free_limit` to at least the size of your biggest expected backlog burst, not the 50 MB default.

code: var perBrokerGb = ingressMBps * retentionSec * rf / brokers / 1000;
Console.WriteLine($"per broker: {perBrokerGb} GB, provision {perBrokerGb * 10 / 7} GB at 70% full");
steps.answer: per broker: 6048 GB, provision 8640 GB at 70% full
explain: 20 x 604 800 x 3 / 6 = 6 048 000 MB, which is 6 048 GB. Dividing by 0.7 (here `* 10 / 7` in integer maths) gives
the disk to buy so the data fills it to 70%.

steps.title: A capacity calculator
prompt: Write the two calculations from the card.
- `long DiskPerBrokerGb(double ingressMBps, double retentionHours, int replicationFactor, int brokers, int maxFillPercent)`:
`ingress x hours x 3600 x RF / brokers / 1000`, scaled to `maxFillPercent` (`x 100 / maxFillPercent`), rounded **up**.
Compute it in exactly that order.
- `string ConsumerPlan(double peakPerSec, double perConsumerPerSec, int partitions)`: `need = ceil(peak / perConsumer)`,
at least 1. If `need <= partitions` → `"run {need} consumers"`, otherwise
`"need {need} consumers but only {partitions} partitions: add partitions or make the handler faster"`.
starter: long DiskPerBrokerGb(double ingressMBps, double retentionHours, int replicationFactor, int brokers, int maxFillPercent)
string ConsumerPlan(double peakPerSec, double perConsumerPerSec, int partitions)
solution: long DiskPerBrokerGb(double ingressMBps, double retentionHours, int replicationFactor, int brokers, int maxFillPercent)
var gb = ingressMBps * retentionHours * 3600 * replicationFactor / brokers / 1000;
string ConsumerPlan(double peakPerSec, double perConsumerPerSec, int partitions)
: $"need {need} consumers but only {partitions} partitions: add partitions or make the handler faster";
hints: `Math.Ceiling` both results; for the disk, multiply by 100 before dividing by the percentage.
`Math.Max(1, ...)` so a quiet topic still gets one consumer.
template: Dojo.Eq("partitions are the ceiling", "need 15 consumers but only 12 partitions: add partitions or make the handler faster", ConsumerPlan(6000, 400, 12));
Dojo.Eq("exactly at the ceiling", "run 12 consumers", ConsumerPlan(4800, 400, 12));

steps.title: Runbooks: lag incident and rebalance storm
body: **Lag incident** (alert: lag in time above SLO and growing)
1. Scope it: `kafka-consumer-groups.sh --describe --group billing`. Lag on **one** partition with a CURRENT-OFFSET that
does not move → a stuck record (poison message, hung call). Lag on **all** partitions → not enough capacity or a
slow dependency.
2. Check the consumer logs and the dependency (database, HTTP API) latency before touching Kafka.
3. Capacity: scale consumers **up to the partition count**; beyond it they idle.
4. Poison record: fix the handler or dead-letter it. Skipping with `--reset-offsets --shift-by 1` is the last resort,
only with the group stopped, and it is a data-loss decision someone owns.
5. Never reset offsets of a group with active members, and never "fix" lag by moving to `--to-latest`.
**Rebalance storm** (the group keeps rebalancing, lag climbs, logs full of revokes)
```text
%4|1764123247.112|MAXPOLL|rdkafka#consumer-1| [thrd:main]: Application maximum poll interval (300000ms) exceeded
by 312ms (adjust max.poll.interval.ms for long-running message processing): leaving group
- The handler took longer than `max.poll.interval.ms` between two `Consume` calls, so the client **left** the group;
its partitions moved, the slow record is redelivered to another member, which also times out: a storm.
- Fixes: put timeouts on every call in the handler; make the slow work smaller or hand it to workers and `Pause`
the partition; raise `MaxPollIntervalMs` consciously when processing really is long; use cooperative-sticky or the
consumer protocol so a single leave does not stop everyone; static membership (`GroupInstanceId`) for restarts.

steps.prompt: billing's lag climbs every few minutes and the logs show the lines below again and again, on different pods. What is the most likely cause?

The topic has too many partitions

`Consume` in time. Heartbeats run on a background thread, so this is not a network problem: it is handler time. Bound

steps.title: Senior's toolkit: operating RabbitMQ and Kafka
steps.body: Reach for these during maintenance and incidents: health and memory checks, safe offset resets, throttled reassignments and rolling restarts.

toolkit.what: Is it up, and are publishers blocked?
What holds the memory (queues, connections, binaries).

toolkit.what: Prefetch and ack mode per consumer.
Would stopping this node cost a quorum queue its majority?
toolkit.when: Run it BEFORE stopping a node.

toolkit.what: One queue's backlog from the management API.

flags: read the NEW-OFFSET column first, then run it again with --execute
bytes/s, so moving replicas does not starve clients

toolkit.when: At the end of every reassignment.

toolkit.what: Move leadership back to the preferred replicas.
Are all replicas back in sync?

steps.prompt: Match each flag or command to what it does.
pairs: Checks the move finished and removes the throttle
Moves leadership back to the preferred replicas
Puts a node in maintenance mode before a restart
Tells you if stopping the node costs a quorum queue its majority

steps.prompt: Move replicas without starving clients, then confirm the move and clear the throttle.
steps.explain: `--generate` only proposes a plan and `--cancel` stops a running move. Forgetting `--verify` leaves the throttle in place long after the move.

steps.prompt: Put the safe replay procedure in order (billing must reprocess everything since 01:00).
lines: Scale the billing consumers to zero
Confirm the group has no active members (`--describe --group billing --state` shows Empty)
Run `--reset-offsets --to-datetime 2026-11-26T01:00:00.000 --dry-run` and read the NEW-OFFSET column
Watch lag drain and the handler's error rate
explain: The reset only works on an inactive group, and the dry run is your chance to catch a wrong topic, partition or
timestamp before it moves anything. The handler must be idempotent: a replay redelivers everything since 01:00.

steps.title: Runbooks: DLQ pile-up and disk full
body: **DLQ pile-up** (`orders.dlq` depth rising)
1. Stop the bleeding: is one release or one dependency causing it? Roll back first, investigate second.
2. Look without losing anything:
```bash
curl -s -u ops:"$RABBIT_PASS" -H 'content-type: application/json' -X POST \
http://rabbit:15672/api/queues/%2F/orders.dlq/get \
-d '{"count":5,"ackmode":"ack_requeue_true","encoding":"auto"}' | jq '.[].properties.headers["x-death"]'
`x-death` tells you the original queue, the reason (`rejected`, `expired`, `maxlen`, `delivery_limit`) and the count.
3. Fix the cause, then replay **slowly** with a shovel back to the original exchange:
`rabbitmqctl set_parameter shovel dlq-replay '{"src-uri":"amqp://","src-queue":"orders.dlq","dest-uri":"amqp://","dest-exchange":"orders","src-delete-after":"queue-length"}'`.
4. Messages that are wrong for good go to a parking-lot queue with a ticket, not back into the loop.
**Broker disk full**
- Kafka: find the biggest partitions with `kafka-log-dirs.sh --describe`; lower `retention.ms` **temporarily** on the
topic that grew (and put it back); add disk or brokers. Never delete segment files by hand on a running broker.
Check for topics with `retention.ms=-1` and for a stalled log cleaner on compacted topics.
- RabbitMQ: the disk alarm blocks all publishers. Free space, drain or purge the queue that grew (after saving what
matters), and set a realistic `disk_free_limit`.

steps.prompt: Match the symptom to the first command you run.
pairs: Lag on one partition, offset not moving
steps.explain: Each first command narrows the problem to one cause without changing anything. Look first, act second.

steps.title: A safe offset reset
prompt: Write the logic of `kafka-consumer-groups.sh --reset-offsets`, so the team's ops bot can show a dry run in chat.
Write `List<string> ResetOffsets(string group, string topic, string state, Dictionary<int, long> current, Dictionary<int, long> logStart, Dictionary<int, long> logEnd, string spec, bool execute)`.
- If `state` is not `"Empty"` or `"Dead"`, return only
`"Error: Assignments can only be reset if the group '{group}' is inactive, but the current state is {state}."`
- `spec` is one of `"--to-earliest"`, `"--to-latest"`, `"--shift-by N"` (N may be negative), `"--to-offset N"`;
- For every partition of `current`, ascending: compute the target, **clamp** it into `[logStart, logEnd]`, and add
- Only when `execute` is true, write the new offsets into `current`. A dry run changes nothing.
starter: List<string> ResetOffsets(string group, string topic, string state, Dictionary<int, long> current,
Dictionary<int, long> logStart, Dictionary<int, long> logEnd, string spec, bool execute)
solution: List<string> ResetOffsets(string group, string topic, string state, Dictionary<int, long> current,
Dictionary<int, long> logStart, Dictionary<int, long> logEnd, string spec, bool execute)
return new List<string> { $"Error: Assignments can only be reset if the group '{group}' is inactive, but the current state is {state}." };
["--shift-by", var n] when long.TryParse(n, out var shift) => p => current[p] + shift,
["--to-offset", var n] when long.TryParse(n, out var offset) => p => offset,
foreach (var (p, next) in plan) current[p] = next;
hints: Check the state first and return the error line before parsing anything.
Turn the spec into a `Func<int, long>` that gives the raw target for a partition, then `Math.Clamp(target, start, end)`.
Build the whole plan first; only copy it into `current` when `execute` is true.

Dojo.Eq("to-latest", new List<string> { "billing orders 0 200", "billing orders 1 6000", "billing orders 2 1000" },
